# Publishing

The publication tool is `tools/publish_collections.py`. It turns each checked-in
collection export into the exact v1 archive accepted by CallersCompendium PR
#1007, derives the manifest measurements from those generated bytes, and signs
the manifest only after all checks pass.

Run the unsigned local gate with:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py' -v
python3 tools/publish_collections.py --no-sign --output /tmp/analect-site
```

The Pages workflow generates the feed in a protected `sign` job using the
`signing` environment, which supplies the maintainer-held
`ANALECT_SIGNING_KEY_B64` secret. The generated Pages artifact is then passed to
a dependent `deploy` job using the standard `github-pages` environment. The
decoded key value may be PEM, DER, or a raw Ed25519 seed, base64-encoded as a
whole (a PEM pasted as-is is not valid base64). Missing credentials, an invalid
key, or a key that does not derive `PINNED_PUBLIC_KEY` in
`tools/publish_collections.py` are hard failures.

## Trust model

The **manifest** is signed with a detached **Ed25519** signature over its exact
bytes, verified in the app against a **pinned set of public keys**. The
manifest carries a **SHA-256 for each archive**, so one signature transitively covers all
published content. Archives are not signed individually.

The signing key is **separate from the key that signs application updates**. The
update key signs installers; sharing it would mean a compromise of collection
publishing could become code execution on every user's machine.

The app pins a **set**: the *current* key this repository signs with, and a
*next* key generated offline and pinned ahead of time (CallersCompendium#2161).
A rotation therefore never ships a release that pins only the replacement key,
which would reject the live catalog, and never switches the signer before the
next key is widely installed, which would strand every older install. The
next key reaches users only with the first app release after `v0.10.0-beta`,
so step 1 has not happened yet and step 2 must not run until that release is
widely installed. In order:

1. A CallersCompendium release adds the next key after the current one. This
   repository keeps signing with the current key.
2. Once that release is widespread, replace the `ANALECT_SIGNING_KEY_B64`
   secret with the next private key **first**, then merge the change that
   updates `PINNED_PUBLIC_KEY` to match. That push re-runs the Pages workflow
   by itself, because `tools/publish_collections.py` is in its `paths`.
   Changing only one of the two fails the publish rather than shipping a
   catalog the app rejects.
3. A later app release drops the old key and pins a new next one.

The full procedure, including custody, where the next key is kept, and what to
do on a compromise, is the app repository's
[published-collection key runbook](https://github.com/ibanner56/CallersCompendium/blob/main/docs/dev/releasing.md#signing-the-published-collection-catalog-ed25519-issue-2161).

## Immutability

A published collection is never edited or deleted. Corrections ship as a new
version under a visible suffix, and the manifest records supersession.

This is what lets a digest stay valid indefinitely, spares every collection from
re-signing, and keeps a user's record of what they imported permanently true.

The visible directory suffix is part of the identity. `collections/foda-1-1`
publishes collection id `foda-1` as SemVer `1.0.0`; changing either the archive or
its identity requires a new directory. `supersedes` must name an older version
of the same collection that is present in the generated feed.

## The v1 archive boundary

The generated archive contains dances and their referenced choreographers. The
following are refused when non-empty: programs, venues, published sources, tags,
top-level custom fields, dance custom-field values, and source citations.
Unknown top-level entities, missing or duplicate dance ids, unreferenced or
missing choreographers, and embedded published-collection provenance also fail.

The source export may contain app-ingestion metadata (`publishedSources`,
`sourceCitations`, and non-published `provenance`); the generator explicitly
maps those fields out because v1 has no transactional source namespace. It never
maps out commentary or custom-field content to make a check pass.

Collections that contain composite phrase structures must declare
`compositePhraseStructureV1` in `requiresCapabilities`. The generator checks
the archive content and propagates this capability into the signed manifest.

## Permission and licence coverage

CI fails a collection that carries written commentary — `hook`, `callingNotes`,
`walkthrough`, or free-text custom fields — **without** a permission or licence
declaration.

The gate **fails**; it does not silently strip. A strip would let a contributor
believe they had published notes that had in fact vanished.

Note what the gate can and cannot do. It checks that a declaration **was made**,
is **well formed**, and **covers the fields actually present**. It cannot check
that the claim is true — a human reviewer must still agree. A green check is not
a legal opinion.

The signed entry carries `grantor`, `holder`, `basis`, `license`, and exhaustive
`fields`; `permission.license` is required to equal the entry's `license`.
Every populated commentary field must be named. Custom-field content is always a
hard failure in v1, even when a declaration exists.

## Manifest schema

The **app repository owns the schema**; its parser is the spec of record. This
repository vendors it.

Parsing **ignores unrecognised fields** and refuses only on an explicit **major**
version bump. This matters because producer and consumer are in different
repositories on independent release cadences: the app's *update* manifest can
safely demand an exact version match because its producer and consumer ship
together, but that same strictness here would mean a schema bump silently
stopped every already-installed app from seeing any collection at all.

A published collection should therefore state the minimum schema version it
requires.

## Generated artifact and site publishing

The Pages artifact contains:

```
collections/manifest.json
collections/manifest.json.sig
collections/<immutable-version>/archive.json
```

The manifest and archives are served from the exact HTTPS origin
`https://analect.callerscompendium.com`, with no query or fragment in archive
URLs. Archive byte size, lowercase SHA-256, and dance count are calculated from
the files written into the Pages artifact.

`site/` deploys via `actions/deploy-pages`, where the artifact is the complete
published state.

The app repository deliberately does the opposite — a branch push that preserves
files it does not own — because two independent writers share its `gh-pages`
branch. This repository has no such split, so the simpler flow is correct here.

**One consequence to respect:** because the artifact *is* the published state,
anything not in it is dropped. `site/CNAME` must therefore stay tracked in this
repository — a custom domain set only in repo settings will be cleared by the
next deploy. See CallersCompendium#863 for the same bug caught in the app repo.
